title: Follow the smart money: 2 tech stocks billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller just bought
summary: Druckenmiller's family office boosted two tech stakes. See what the 13F data shows and what investors can't see in it.
content: Every quarter, investors get a peek at what some of Wall Street’s best-known names own. When a famous investor increases exposure to a stock, people are bound to take notice. Billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller’s latest snapshot has two such moves. In one tech company, his firm’s share count jumped more than fivefold. In another, it nearly tripled. One company helps people build video games, and the other is a data storage company. Both companies expect artificial intelligence to help drive revenue higher over the next few years. Who is Stanley Druckenmiller? Druckenmiller is a billionaire investor and former hedge fund manager. He founded Duquesne Capital Management in 1981 and ran it until 2010, according to his CNBC profile . Also Read: Stanley Druckenmiller dumps entire $120M Alphabet stake to buy gold mining stock He also spent more than a decade at George Soros’ firm, where he was lead portfolio manager of the well-known Quantum Fund. Today, Druckenmiller is chairman and chief investment officer of Duquesne Family Office, according to Bloomberg . Large money managers must list certain holdings every quarter on Form 13F. The report is due within 45 days after the quarter ends, according to the Securities and Exchange Commission . Unity stock is a sizable bet Unity Software led Duquesne’s percentage increases in the 13F data reviewed. The investment firm added 3.2 million shares in Q3, an increase of 436% year over year. The position is worth $161.9 million or 3.66% of the total portfolio. Unity (U) offers tools for building games and also runs an ad business that helps publishers find players. Its engine is Unity Vector, an AI system that predicts which games users are likely to engage with. More Wall Street: Arista Networks stock gets fresh backing from Jim Cramer and Wall Street Oracle stock sinks as Wall Street confronts a $20 billion AI problem Wall Street just got a candid look at who is winning the AI race Valued at a market cap of $21.4 billion, Unity stock is down 74% from all-time highs but continues to grow at a steady pace. In Q3, it reported : Strategic revenue, a headline company measure, of $597 million, an increase of 59% year over year Vector revenue growth of 126% YoY and 40% sequentially GAAP net income of $122 million Record free cash flow of $220 million CEO Matt Bromberg wants investors to see beyond ads and emphasized. “We are not an ad network. We are an authoring platform.” Bromberg calls its business model a flywheel, which starts with making games easier to create with AI. This, in turn, attracts more creators who launch more games and make more use of Unity’s tools. But more games bring a new headache, which is getting noticed. As the shelves get crowded, publishers have a greater need to reach the right players, which should drive demand for the ad business. AI may also shorten the path between those two steps. In the past, developers had to seek out Vector, download its software, and set it up. In the new world of building through AI prompts, Bromberg says Vector and other Unity services connect as soon as a game is created. Unity’s daily active users have risen 25% since early August, when it opened its platform to AI coding agents. For the fourth quarter, Unity expects strategic revenue to grow 65% to 67% from the prior year. It sees Vector rising 21% to 23% from the third quarter, and Bromberg cautioned that not every quarter will bring 40% growth. Given estimates compiled by TIKR , analysts forecast free cash flow to expand from $404 million in 2025 to $2.7 billion in 2030. If Unity stock is priced at 20x forward FCF, it could surge 157% within the next three years. Stanley Druckenmiller, CEO of Duquesne Family Office, raises its stake in Unity and Seagate. Bloomberg / Getty Images Seagate stock rides the data boom Seagate Technology (STX) is the larger of the two positions. Duquesne’s stake climbed from 122,000 shares to 341,790, up 180.16%. The holding is worth more than $300 million and accounts for 7% of the portfolio. Together, Seagate and Unity make up almost 11% of the total portfolio. Seagate makes hard drives, and big data centers drive top-line demand. Its case is simple: AI creates and reuses huge amounts of data, which needs to be stored. In fiscal Q1 (ended in September), revenue rose 61% year over year to $4.2 billion, while adjusted earnings almost tripled to $7.68 per share. Adjusted gross margin rose to 57.8% from 52.7% in the prior quarter. Related: Seagate’s booming business comes with an unexpected twist Customers are also planning far ahead. Most of Seagate’s supply of high-capacity data center storage is already allocated under long-term agreements through calendar 2028. CEO Dave Mosley sees more room to run. “We believe we’re still in the early days of a multiyear growth phase,” he said on the Oct. 27 call. For the December quarter, Seagate expects about $4.8 billion in revenue, give or take $100 million. The midpoint implies 70% yearly growth. It also expects adjusted earnings of $9.20 per share, plus or minus 20 cents. EPS is projected to more than double from $40 in fiscal 2027 to $84 in 2029. If the tech stock is priced at 10 times earnings, it could surge 80% within the next two years. What 13F filings don’t tell investors Before you follow the smart money, remember that a 13F looks in the rearview mirror. The data here don’t show what Duquesne paid, why it bought, or whether it still owns these shares. However, the two tech stocks continue to grow at a stellar rate and are expanding profit margins and cash flow. Treat Druckenmiller’s moves as a starting point for research, then weigh the risks yourself. title: Target cut its Apple Black Friday discount in half
summary: There are two Target rules customers should know before buying.
content: Target is promoting its 2026 Black Friday event as an expanded eight-day sale, but shoppers looking for major discounts on flagship electronics will notice smaller price cuts than last year. The Minneapolis-based retail giant launched its main Black Friday sale on Sunday, Nov. 22, running through Sunday, Nov. 29. That schedule adds one extra day compared with its seven-day event in 2025. Behind the broader promotion, however, Target scaled back the headline ceiling on some of its most-searched holiday tech items. Target cuts Apple Black Friday savings in half In its official holiday announcement , Target said shoppers can save “up to $100 on select Apple devices” during its Black Friday event. That is half the maximum discount Target advertised during Black Friday 2025, when Apple savings topped out at $200 off select products, according to an analysis by Digital Citizen and Target’s official 2025 holiday announcement . Target’s current sale includes markdowns on specific Apple device and accessories: Apple AirPods Pro 3: Marked down to $149.99 from $249.99 , a $100 discount. Apple Watch Series 12 (42mm GPS): Reduced to $299.99 from $399.99 , also hitting the $100 ceiling. 11-inch Apple iPad (A16, 128GB): Discounted by $70 to $379.99 . Source: Target’s Weekly Ad (with price reported on the morning of November 26) At the same time, a major gaming discount vanished from Target’s Black Friday lineup. Last year, the retailer advertised a flat $100 off PlayStation 5 consoles. Target cut its Apple Black Friday discount in half. Bloomberg / Getty Images In 2026, Target’s Black Friday announcement omitted PlayStation consoles entirely, highlighting gaming deals on Nintendo, Nex, and Meta Quest instead. While Target discounted DualSense PS5 controllers by $20 to $64.99, console buyers will not find last year’s $100 markdown. There is one quiet exception in Target’s live Black Friday lineup. Despite advertising a $100 ceiling in its press release, Target discounted Apple AirPods Max 2 by $120, dropping the over-ear headphones to $429.99 from $549.99, according to Target’s product listing , though Amazon and Best Buy still undercut that price by $10, per NBC News Select . Why Target is holding back on deep tech markdowns Target enters the 2026 holiday weekend in a much stronger financial position than it held a year ago. In its third-quarter earnings report released Nov. 18, Target posted a 7.1% jump in net sales and a 5.6% increase in comparable sales, according to Target’s Q3 2026 financial release . Customer traffic rose 5% year over year, reversing a 2.2% traffic decline during the same quarter in 2025. Because shoppers are already returning to Target stores and digital channels, the chain raised its full-year sales outlook. Jefferies analysts said in a note this month that Target’s recent price cuts and focus on newness have been bringing customers back, according to Retail Dive . That momentum may leave Target with less need for aggressive loss-leader console or Apple discounts to get customers through the door. Across retail, many companies are also holding leaner inventories after tariff disruptions to protect margins, which leaves less excess stock to clear at deep discounts, University of Miami professor Claudia Townsend told NBC News Select . Instead, Target is spreading promotional dollars across mass-traffic giveaways and everyday categories. On Black Friday morning, Nov. 27, stores open at 6 a.m. local time and will hand out gift cards worth $25, $50, or $100 to the first 100 shoppers in line, including one $1,000 gift card per store, according to Target’s Black Friday press release . Meanwhile, competitors are still using higher Apple ceilings to pull tech shoppers away. Best Buy launched its Black Friday sale on Nov. 19 with up to $250 off select MacBook Air models, while Amazon also advertised discounts exceeding $100 on higher-end Apple hardware. Knowing where rivals beat Target is only half the equation; shoppers also need to watch how consumer buying habits are shifting this week and check two strict Target rules before buying. Related: Shoppers ditch Hostess snack cakes while Uncrustables sell faster than factories can make them Shoppers are using Black Friday differently in 2026 Even when retailers trim headline tech discounts, Americans are still planning to spend heavily over Thanksgiving weekend, though what they put in their carts is changing. Nearly two-thirds of U.S. consumers, or 64%, say they are likely to wait until Thanksgiving weekend to do most of their holiday shopping, up from 51% five years ago, according to the National Retail Federation . Overall holiday retail sales are projected to grow 4.2% to $1.013 trillion. At the same time, budget-conscious households are using Cyber Week sales to stock up on everyday necessities alongside gifts. Online sales of personal hygiene products are projected to jump 150% during Cyber Week, compared with September levels, as shoppers hunt for deals on clothing basics, household cleaning supplies, and daily essentials, according to Adobe’s 2026 Holiday Shopping Report . That shift plays directly into Target’s core strengths in apparel, beauty, and household goods, where the retailer is still offering up to 50% off apparel and accessories, 40% off beauty and health gift sets, and 50% off decorative pillows and throws during its Nov. 26–29 weekend wave. Two Target rules shoppers should know before purchasing If you still plan to buy electronics at Target this weekend, whether for convenience or to stack an extra 5% discount with a Target Circle Card, pay close attention to two policies that can save or cost you money: Use the Holiday Price Match Guarantee: Any eligible item purchased at Target between Nov. 1 and Dec. 24 qualifies for a price adjustment if Target lowers its own price later in the season, TheStreet previously reported . Keep your receipt or Circle account record in case Cyber Monday or December flash deals drop prices further. Watch the shorter Apple return clock: Target gives most electronics and entertainment purchases a generous return window starting Dec. 26. However, Apple and Beats products, along with unlocked or prepaid phones, have only a 14-day holiday return window, meaning items bought for Christmas must be returned by Jan. 8, 2027, rather than Jan. 24 for standard electronics, as noted by Digital Citizen . Checking competitor prices on big-ticket Apple devices and noting that early January deadlines can help shoppers avoid overpaying, or getting stuck with an unreturnable gift, during the busiest shopping weekend of the year. title: Thanksgiving airfares jumped 57% as a new travel risk emerges
summary: Americans are paying sharply higher airfares, but recent airline disruptions are giving some travelers another reason to stay off planes.
content: Rising ticket prices have made Thanksgiving travel more expensive for millions of Americans, but some families are reconsidering their holiday flights for other reasons. Driving has become a more appealing option due to a number of flight problems, especially for passengers on trips that might take longer than ten hours. Reuters reported Wednesday, Nov. 25, that domestic Thanksgiving airfares averaged approximately $469 two weeks before the holiday, a 57% increase from the comparable period last year, according to travel search engine Kayak. The significant increase coincides with rising fuel prices, concerns about flight reliability, and a strong Thanksgiving storm for airlines. The Federal Aviation Administration’s nationwide ground stop on Nov. 13, triggered by a technical failure, added to those concerns, disrupting air travel across the country. For some travelers, the convenience of flying is now outweighed by the possibility of another setback. However, Americans are hardly giving up on traveling for Thanksgiving. Just under the previous year’s record of 81.6 million, AAA predicts that 81.5 million people will travel at least 50 miles from home during the holiday season. The travel sector faces a glaring contradiction as a result. Although Americans are becoming more conscious of the cost and dependability of travel, they still wish to see friends and family. The problem for airlines goes beyond just selling pricey tickets. They have to convince passengers that flying is still worth the extra cost and risk. Thanksgiving airfares hit their highest levels in a decade The cost of air travel has become a significant barrier for families planning vacations. Thanksgiving and Christmas fares are at their highest levels in ten years, according to Reuters, partially due to rising jet fuel prices. Although its numbers differ from Kayak’s, AAA’s independent study confirms the pressure. Travelers paid an average of $800 for domestic round-trip Thanksgiving tickets, up 17% from 2025, according to AAA’s Nov. 16 projection. The difference matters. Kayak’s 57% increase measures fares advertised at a particular point before Thanksgiving, while AAA’s 17% increase reflects tickets travelers had already booked. The figures are not directly comparable. Fuel prices are another issue that airlines must deal with. Industry group Airlines for America said jet fuel prices averaged $4.64 per gallon in October, setting a record. Carriers have responded by reducing some flight frequencies, retiring older aircraft, and increasing certain fees. Higher ticket costs are particularly upsetting to customers when multiple family members need to travel together. FAA’s nationwide disruption adds another warning Ticket prices are just one issue. Flights were halted nationwide Nov. 13 after a technical failure destabilized air traffic communications systems. The disruption started around 3:30 p.m., the agency said. Eastern and normal air traffic resumed at 8:15 p.m. The FAA reported 12,462 flight cancellations that day, but not all were due to the ground stop. In the days that followed, United Airlines (UAL) and Delta Air Lines (DAL) experienced more technical issues. Another issue arose on Thursday due to severe weather. The organization projects the following figures for Nov. 24 through Nov. 30: 72.9 million Americans traveling by car, down from 73.1 million last year. 5.96 million traveling by domestic air, a 0.2% decline. 2.6 million using buses, trains and cruises, an increase of 4.1%. 81.5 million total travelers, compared with 81.6 million in 2025. For nearly 90% of Thanksgiving travelers, driving remains their top choice. Road excursions are not exempt from rising expenses due to rising gas prices. Interest is also growing in other transit providers. On the day of the FAA interruption, bookings on travel platform Wanderu increased by almost 16%, while bus operator Flix North America reported a 17% spike in Thanksgiving reservations, according to a Reuters story on Wednesday. Amtrak, meanwhile, expects another strong Thanksgiving season after recording 1.2 million passenger trips during the holiday period last year. These changes suggest that passengers are seeking alternatives, even though overall AAA statistics do not show a national increase in driving compared with the previous year. What the Thanksgiving travel shift means for airlines Major US carriers must perform a challenging balancing act amid an evolving travel landscape. Airlines for America expects approximately 29 million passengers between Nov. 20 and Nov. 30. American Airlines (AAL) expects over 8 million passengers, while United expects over 6.6 million during its Thanksgiving travel period. Airlines have planned more capacity despite worries about demand. Flight analytics company Cirium estimates that US carriers are operating approximately 2% more flights than last Thanksgiving, with seat capacity increasing 1%, Reuters reported. Turning such capacity into profitable travel while controlling fuel prices and operational disruptions is the airlines’ problem. Price-conscious consumers may be turned off by higher ticket prices, even though they might help offset costs. Travelers are making decisions that go beyond simply comparing tickets. Reliability, overall costs, and the possibility of missing Thanksgiving festivities are now major factors. Although there is still strong demand for vacation travel, the industry’s most recent data show a significant shift. Americans are still committed to getting where they want to go.
